title: A coherent common generic lattice of two integral ideals
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $i:W\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $W$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Let $I,J$ be quasi-coherent ideals represented by $W.\mathrm{IdealSheafData}$ with $i_*I$ nonzero [def-pc-module-pullback] and $J\ne 0$. The pushforward $i_*I$ is coherent, and there exist a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $K$ [pqf-def-coherent] and monomorphisms $b:K\to i_*J$ and $d:K\to i_*I$ such that both maps on module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] at $i(\operatorname{genericPoint}(W))$ are isomorphisms. No assertion about cokernels is made.

source.place: Tag 01YH, lemma-property-irreducible, proof: intersection comparison in the paragraph beginning Next, suppose

proof.text: The zero ideal has zero affine sections, hence a zero module; pushforward preserves zero objects. Thus nonzero i_*I implies I is nonzero. W is locally Noetherian as a closed subscheme. Quasi-coherence of ideals follows from their kernel construction; coherent submodule closure inside the coherent structure module gives coherence of I.

Construct L as the kernel of I -> O_W -> (W/J)_* O_(W/J). Its kernel arrow b_0 embeds it into I. The composite b_0 followed by I -> O_W lifts to J by the universal property of the kernel defining J. Its composite with J -> O_W is b_0 followed by I -> O_W, so the lift d_0 is mono. L is quasi-coherent and is a submodule of coherent I, hence coherent. This kernel is the actual intersection, without selecting an existence witness.

Both ideals have full generic stalk. The generic map O_W -> (W/J)_* O_(W/J) is zero because its composite with the surjective generic inclusion of J is zero. Stalk exactness of the kernel sequence then makes b_0 surjective and injective at the generic point. The equality of the two composites and bijectivity of both ideal inclusions make d_0 bijective too. Push forward L and the two maps; finite pushforward preserves coherence and monomorphisms. Naturality of the bijective closed-pushforward stalk comparison transfers the two generic bijections.

lean.statement:
theorem integral_ideals_common_generic_lattice {X W : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] (i : W ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsIntegral W]
    (I J : W.IdealSheafData) (hI : ¬ IsZero ((pushforward i).obj I.toModules))
    (hJ : J ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ (K : X.Modules) (b : K ⟶ (pushforward i).obj J.toModules)
      (d : K ⟶ (pushforward i).obj I.toModules),
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace ((pushforward i).obj I.toModules) ∧
      RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace K ∧ Mono b ∧ Mono d ∧
      IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
        (i.base (genericPoint W))).map b) ∧
      IsIso ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace
        (i.base (genericPoint W))).map d)
